question: A communications team wants every press-release draft produced in a shared project to come out in the company's house voice, without anyone having to explain the voice again in each chat. What should the team do first?
options: A) Ask Claude in each new chat to match the house voice, and then correct the tone in the follow-up messages each time.
B) Write down the house voice rules and audience the team already applies, then put them in the project instructions.
C) Upload every press release published last year and let Claude infer the house voice on its own from them.
D) Create a separate project for each writer so that every person can keep their own preferred tone settings.
correct_answers: B) Write down the house voice rules and audience the team already applies, then put them in the project instructions.
explanations: This is the repeated one-off prompting the team is trying to escape, and it produces different results per person.
Correct. The durable direction has to exist as agreed wording before it can be configured; defining what good looks like comes first.
Samples are useful background, but they do not state the rules, and inference from mixed past work is unreliable.
This guarantees inconsistency, which is the opposite of the shared house voice the team asked for.
